answer: Recent human evidence is largely observational, reporting associations rather than confirmed clinical outcomes [2]. Studies have reported possible associations between microplastics in the body and gastrointestinal complications, inflammatory conditions, hormonal imbalances, and reproductive dysfunction [2]. Microplastics may induce inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, and cellular damage, contributing to various diseases [2]. Their synergistic effects with other environmental pollutants may amplify adverse health outcomes [1]. Direct evidence linking mechanisms such as endocrine disruption and gut microbiota alterations to adverse human outcomes remains limited [2].
